co_sailing_hawks.blurb: Sailing Hawks lies just north of Durango, in the Dalla Mountain Park trail network along the foot of Animas Mountain. The rock is sandstone, and boulders make up the great bulk of the climbing, with a few trad, sport and top-rope lines mixed in around the edges. Problems run from V0 up to V12, but the weight sits in the easy and middle grades, V0 to V6, so there is plenty for newer boulderers as well as a thin top end. The roped climbs are mostly 5.9 to 5.12. The ground is very spread out, split into dozens of small clusters such as Loiterland, Petrified Area, Pocket Change Area and Quantum Boulder. Durango's climbing season generally runs spring through fall.

az_crags_along_the_peavine_trail.blurb: These crags sit in the Granite Dells just outside Prescott, at roughly 5,200 feet, and are strung along a long trail beside Watson Lake. The Dells are rounded formations of medium-grained desert granite, grainy on some of them. Trad is the main event, with a smaller share of sport and a few top-rope lines. Grades run from about 5.5 to 5.12, with the heaviest concentration around 5.10, so solid mid-grade leaders have the most to climb, though moderates are present too. The big names here are The Notch, Canyon Wren Canyon, Easter Peak, Point of Rocks and Upper Boulder Creek, and many other walls and domes hold only a handful of lines each.

va_boneyard_area.blurb: The Boneyard is a big boulderfield on the mountainside within Grayson Highlands State Park, to the right of the A.V.P. boulders. Everything here is bouldering, from VB up to about V9, with the bulk of problems between V0 and V5. The stone is a fairly sharp metamorphic sandstone, and the problems lean toward slopey top-outs and pinchy, pumping moves. The blocks are scattered widely enough that it can feel uncrowded even on a busy day. It divides into Left, Middle and Right Boneyard, plus the A.V.P. Boulders and Garden Boulders. The park's boulder fields mostly sit between about 4,500 and 4,900 feet, and the park is known for good summer bouldering.

va_listening_rock_trail.blurb: Listening Rock Trail is one of the three main boulder fields in Grayson Highlands State Park, and for many visitors it holds the park's best bouldering. The approach is very short, and the loop winds past most of the main boulders. Every climb here is a boulder problem, from VB to about V11, with most of the volume between V0 and V4 and a steady tail of harder problems above. Sub-areas include Overlook Area, SLS Area, Moonlight, Central and Trails End Area, the last of which sits at the far end of the loop, sees lighter traffic and has a lot of easy lines. The park's high boulder fields, roughly 4,500 to 4,900 feet, are noted for good summer conditions.

wa_glacier_peak_region.blurb: Darrington sits on the west slope of the Cascades, about 30 miles east of I-5, and most of the climbing here is on granite domes in the Clear Creek and Squire Creek drainages south of town. The rock is generally clean, and routes are often multi-pitch, many leading to a summit. Bolts turn up, but a rack is usually needed, so trad dominates; sport, bouldering and some alpine and scrambling objectives fill out the rest. Grades are mostly 5.8 to 5.10, with some harder. Exfoliation Dome, Three O'Clock Rock and Spring Mountain are among the better-known walls. Rainfall here is two to three times Seattle's, the forest is thick, and routes can stay damp for a day or two after a long wet spell.

ma_the_promised_land.blurb: The Promised Land is a bouldering area in Lynn Woods on Massachusetts' North Shore, low-lying at around 130 feet. The blocks are granite, roughly 10 to 20 feet tall, gathered into about 40 small clusters that are a short walk from one another. Nearly all of the climbing is bouldering, with only a few roped lines. The area is organised into two sectors, Sector One and Sector Two. Problems span V0 to V10, with the densest concentration in the V4 to V8 range, and the easier end is still being filled in. It feels like a hidden pocket of boulders tucked into the woods.
